title: Sierra Tech - Security & Deployment Q&A
summary: Discovery focused on compliance posture (SOC 2 / ISO), SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logging needs, KMS/encryption model options for hosted vs private, and data retention/deletion SLAs. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to regulatory data residency and corporate policy. Next steps: send SOC2 + ISO docs, architecture diagram for VPC/private deployment, draft pilot pricing for a 3-month Dedicated pool, schedule technical POC for on-prem feasibility.
topics: Encryption at rest / KMS / HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Samir to share SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 coverage matrix (by 2026-01-03)
Priya to produce VPC/private deployment diagram with recommended firewall/nat topology (by 2026-01-07)
Sales to circulate Dedicated pilot pricing and SLA options for 3-month trial (by 2025-12-31)
Schedule SE-led POC to test KMS integration and E2E audit log export (tentative week of 2026-01-13)
action_items: Samir - Send SOC2 report + redacted pen test summary - due 2026-01-03
Priya - VPC private deployment diagram + KV cache behavior notes - due 2026-01-07
Jamie (Customer) - Share compliance questionnaire and list of in-scope datasets - due 2026-01-05
Elena - Coordinate POC schedule and send calendar invites - due 2025-12-30
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-28 16:00 UTC | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood CSM), Tom (Sierra CTO), Maya (Sierra Security), Jamie (Sierra Infra), Elliot (Procurement)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Samir, AE on the Redwood account. Priya is our solutions engineer, Elena handles post-sales. Tom, Maya, Jamie, Elliot thanks for making time.
[00:20] Tom (Sierra CTO): Yep thanks. We wanted to use this as a deep Q&A; we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated and probably private in the long run. security posture is main blocker.
[00:32] Maya (Security Lead): Right, we need SOC2 and ISO evidence, SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC model for least privilege, and full audit logs with immutability. Also KMS integration - we have a corporate HSM for keys, so key rotation and no-key-extract requirements.
[00:55] Priya (Redwood SE): Totally understood. I can walk through our options. For Hosted API customers, we provide SOC2 Type II and we do have an ISO 27001-certified control set — I'll attach the docs. For encryption, hosted can use Redwood-managed KMS or customer-managed KMS in some tiers. For Dedicated and Private we support bring-your-own-key via customer KMS and HSM integrations.
[01:20] Maya: When you say "support", does that mean keys never leave our HSM? We have a hard requirement that plaintext keys not be exported.
[01:30] Priya: Correct — with Private (and certain Dedicated configurations) the keys stay in your KMS/HSM. Redwood calls the integration via Cloud KMS APIs and we don't persist key material. The calls are KMS Encrypt/Decrypt in-line; nothing stored locally as plaintext.
[01:47] Jamie (Infra): Is that true for both GCP KMS and AWS KMS? We run a hybrid.
[01:54] Priya: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for Private and Dedicated. There are some extra steps for cross-cloud networking for Private on-prem but it's supported.
[02:05] Elliot (Procurement): Pricing question: does BYOK add cost? And what about HSM fees?
[02:12] Samir: Good questions. BYOK is usually included at higher-tier Dedicated/private plans; HSMs are billed by the customer's cloud provider for HSM usage. Redwood won't charge extra for the integration itself, but there can be engineering setup fees for on-prem installations. We'll put that in the pilot quote.
[02:30] Tom: Ok. Audit logs — we need immutable logs with at least 1 year retention, exportable to our SIEM. Can Redwood push logs to our Splunk/Datadog/S3?
[02:41] Priya: Yes. We can stream audit logs to your S3 bucket, and we have integrations to forward to Splunk/Datadog. For Hosted we retain logs for X days by default (we'll show the retention table), Dedicated/Private you control retention in the console and we support long-term export. Immutability — we can append-only write to S3 with lifecycle rules and we also provide an HMAC-signed audit manifest if you want tamper-evidence.
[03:05] Maya: HMAC-signed manifest is good. Are audit events at token level or request level? We need user-level actionability — who requested what prompt, which model, input redaction policies for PII.
[03:17] Priya: We log request metadata: requestor identity (via SSO token), model, route, latency, tokens in/out counts. For inputs we have redaction tooling; we don't store raw PII in the audit log unless you opt in during the POC — default is redacted.
[03:35] Tom: Can we reconstitute request payloads for debugging if needed?
[03:40] Priya: With explicit opt-in and SAML-backed consent + tenant policy, yes; otherwise no. We'll include the policy language.
[03:48] [00:04:00] Speaker 3: Uh, just a note — transcription might say KV cash instead of KV cache, ignore that.
[03:55] Jamie: On RBAC, we want least privilege per team and per-route controls. e.g., only the payments team can call models with PII-sensitive routes and only through dedicated nodes. How granular is RBAC?
[04:08] Priya: RBAC is role-and-policy based — you can create roles scoped to model, route, and environment. For Dedicated/Private you get per-token tracing and token-level cost visibility. You can map your SAML groups to roles via SCIM. Cross-tenant isolation is enforced at the infra layer for Dedicated pools.
[04:26] Maya: Do you have attestations for RBAC enforcement? We need logs proving policy evaluation and deny/allow decisions.
[04:34] Priya: Yes, policy evaluations are logged — we'll include sample logs. For the audit trail we log the policy id, decision, timestamp, and principal.
[04:45] Tom: Data residency — some of our datasets must remain in EU. Does Redwood offer region pinning for Hosted?
[04:53] Samir: Hosted supports region pinning for enterprise customers; otherwise we route to nearest region. Dedicated and Private you control region and placement. For EU-only requirements we'd recommend Dedicated in a EU region or Private on-prem.
[05:05] Maya: For Private deployments, what does the control plane look like? Is telemetry and control plane data ever sent back to Redwood? We're strict about telemetry leaving the VPC.
[05:15] Priya: For Private, there are two modes. Fully air-gapped on-prem where control plane is customer-managed — no telemetry leaves your network. Or semi-managed where control-plane calls telemetry to Redwood for upgrades and billing but you can opt-out of telemetry and run offline upgrade process. We'll provide the control-plane architecture doc.
[05:34] Elliot: Is SSO SAML 2.0 supported? We use Azure AD. Also SCIM provisioning?
[05:40] Priya: Yes to both. SAML 2.0 SSO with Azure AD is first-class; SCIM provisioning for groups/users is supported; we map Azure AD groups to Redwood roles. The SCIM endpoints can be behind your firewall for Private.
[05:53] Jamie: What about session timeout and token lifetime? We want short lived tokens for elevated access.
[05:59] Priya: Token lifetimes are configurable via your IdP claims. For elevated sessions we support time-limited elevation and session revoke through the console and SCIM deprovisioning.
[06:10] [00:08:00] Maya: Key rotation policy — we need quarterly rotation and a proof-of-rotation report tied to our audit. How does Redwood demonstrate KMS rotation if keys are in our HSM?
[06:22] Priya: If keys are in your HSM, rotation is driven by you; Redwood will log the key id used for each envelope and we can include rotation markers in audit logs. For Redwood-managed keys we support configurable rotation cadence and we can provide rotation logs and attestations.
[06:38] Tom: Any SOC2 exclusions? Some vendors carve out infra-level stuff.
[06:43] Samir: SOC2 covers the inference platform and control plane for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private on-prem the SOC2 report documents the Redwood controls but customers are responsible for their on-prem controls — we'll annotate the report with in-scope vs customer-managed items.
[06:58] Maya: Pen test history? Do you do internal and external pentests and when was the last one?
[07:04] Elena (CSM): We do annual third-party pentests and maintain a vulnerability disclosure program. Last third-party pentest completed Q3 2025; we'll share a redacted summary.
[07:13] Maya: Great. Also need SLA for incident response and RTO for Dedicated pools.
[07:20] Samir: SLA varies by plan; Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. For incidents we commit to an on-call RTO and incident notification timeline — we'll include the SLA doc in the follow-up.
[07:31] Tom: Latency trade-offs — our app is latency-sensitive for synchronous use. If we choose Dedicated versus Hosted what's typical p95 improvement?
[07:40] Priya: Dedicated puts you on reserved GPU pools which removes noisy neighbors and can cut p95 by 30-60% depending on model and batch. We'll include benchmark sheets showing p50/p95 for common model families. For strict SLAs we recommend Dedicated with pinned models and warm KV caching.
[07:58] Jamie: Warm KV cache — how do you manage cache eviction and multitenancy concerns? We can't have data leakage across tenants.
[08:07] Priya: KV cache is namespaced per tenant; eviction policies are configurable. We never colocate tenant caches in a way that would cause leakages; for Private, cache is fully tenant-local.
[08:20] [00:12:00] Elliot: Procurement - what about contract terms: data processing agreement, liability caps, breach notification?
[08:27] Samir: We include DPA, standard liability caps in enterprise agreements, and breach notification timelines. We'll have legal review and share redlines.
[08:36] Maya: Data retention and deletion — we need the ability to purge data on demand, and verifiable deletion certs for certain records. How does Redwood handle retention for inputs, embeddings, and logs?
[08:47] Priya: Default retention: Hosted ephemeral caching for 30 days depending on plan; embeddings and training never persisted unless you opt-in for fine-tuning (we flag that). For Dedicated/Private, retention is customer-configurable and we support on-demand deletes. We can provide a deletion confirmation with a signed timestamp, and for Private on-prem, deletion is local so you control the process.
[09:06] Maya: For embeddings and vector DB caches used in retrieval augmentation, if we configure a persistent cache, can we ensure encrypted at rest and segregated?
[09:15] Priya: Yes — you can configure encryption and storage to tenant buckets. For Hosted if you request long-term storage we can store embeddings in your own S3 with SSE-KMS. For Dedicated/Private it's under your storage controls.
[09:28] Tom: Can we bring our own storage for logs and embeddings?
[09:32] Priya: Yes — S3 or GCS buckets in your account for exports. We'll support lifecycle rules and object lock if you'd like immutability.
[09:41] [00:16:00] Speaker 2: minor audio glitch here, apologies.
[09:44] Jamie: For on-prem Private deployment, what's the typical ops overhead? We want a T-shirt size for engineer time to maintain.
[09:52] Priya: For a standard Private deployment we estimate 1-2 FTEs for day-to-day ops during ramp and 0.5-1 FTEs ongoing depending on your automation. We'll provide a runbook and automation scripts. There's also an initial integration week where Redwood SEs help set up networking, KMS, and monitoring.
[10:10] Tom: Are upgrades automated? We prefer control-plane-controlled upgrades during maintenance windows.
[10:15] Priya: Upgrades can be scheduled; for fully air-gapped installs you run a manual upgrade package. For semi-managed we can push upgrades during your maintenance window with approval.
[10:24] Maya: What about telemetry minimization? We cannot have query-level telemetry for EU-regulated data.
[10:31] Priya: You can opt-out of telemetry; we have a telemetry minimization mode that sends only heartbeat pings and billing metrics. For deeper telemetry you can keep it internal.
[10:40] Elliot: Regarding backups — if we run Private on-prem, who holds backups and what's the restore SLA?
[10:46] Priya: Backups are customer-managed for Private; Redwood provides backup tooling and recommended RPO/RTO. For Dedicated, Redwood manages backups with defined RPOs in the contract.
[10:56] [00:20:00] Samir: Quick recap — main customer asks: SOC2/ISO docs, BYOK/HSM assurances, long-term immutable audit logs with export, SCIM/SAML integration, per-route RBAC, data residency, deletion certs. We'll send docs and propose a Dedicated pilot with a POC to validate KMS integration and audit log export.
[11:17] Tom: Sounds good. For the POC we want a narrow scope: a single EU Dedicated pool, SAML integration with Azure AD, KMS integration with our AWS KMS in eu-west-1, and audit log stream to our S3 + Splunk. Can we get that stood up in two weeks?
[11:34] Priya: Two weeks is tight but possible for a pilot — we'll need access, SCIM info, and an engineer from your side for network setup. We'll confirm dates in the follow-up.
[11:45] Maya: Can you also include a data flow diagram that labels where PII can appear and the redaction points?
[11:52] Priya: Yes, we'll include a data flow + redaction guidance doc.
[11:56] Jamie: Any network ports or firewall rules we should prepare?
[12:00] Priya: We'll send the network checklist — typically requires outbound TLS to our control-plane endpoints and some private peering for Private.
[12:09] [00:24:00] Elliot: For procurement, we might need a draft SOW and PO path in calendar. We'll require a bill-to entity and list of in-scope services.
[12:19] Samir: We'll draft a pilot SOW and include bill-to examples.
[12:24] Tom: One more — model governance: can we pin model versions and restrict who can roll forward? We need change control.
[12:32] Priya: Yes, model pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B, automatic rollback) are in the console. Rollout approval gates can be configured so only specific roles can promote versions. All promotions are logged.
[12:46] Maya: That helps. Also want an incident playbook specific to PII exposure — do you have a runbook?
[12:52] Elena: Yes, we have a PII incident response playbook and notification templates; we'll provide that.
[12:58] [00:28:00] Samir: Anything else from the team?
[13:02] Tom: Not today. We'll review the docs and confirm the POC scope.
[13:06] Maya: We'll compile our compliance questionnaire and share by Monday.
[13:10] Jamie: I'll get networking creds and artisan — sorry, I mean service account details to Samir.
[13:17] Samir: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites.
[13:22] [00:32:00] Closing notes: Transcription may have misheard a few technical terms (KV cache spelled as KV cash) — ignore those.

End of transcript.
